questions.question: What is soil erosion, and how do dongas form?
questions.expected_answer: Soil erosion is the carrying away of soil by water or wind. When heavy rain falls on bare ground, running water carries soil down the slope and cuts small grooves. If nothing stops it, the grooves join and grow into gullies and then into deep ditches called dongas, which grow deeper and wider with every storm.

questions.question: Explain how plants protect soil, and name three human activities that cause erosion.
questions.expected_answer: Leaves break the force of the raindrops, and roots hold the soil together like a net, so soil covered with plants hardly erodes. Human activities that remove plant cover and cause erosion include overgrazing, cutting down trees and bushes, ploughing up and down slopes, wearing paths into slopes, and burning the veld too often.

questions.question: Describe four ways to conserve soil.
questions.expected_answer: Keep soil covered by planting grass and trees; build low stone walls or gabions to slow running water; move cattle so that grass can grow back and avoid overgrazing; plough across slopes, called contour ploughing, or build terraces; plant windbreaks; and cover garden soil with mulch and add compost.
